غَدِرٌ [part. n. of غَدِرَ]. ―
-b2- See غَادِرٌ, last sentence but one. ＝
-A2- And see also غَدُورٌ. ＝
-A3- You say also لَيْلَةٌ غَدِرَةٌ and ↓ مُغْدِرَةٌ (S, K) meaning A dark night; (K;) as also ↓ غَدْرَآءُ : (IKtt, TA:) or an intensely-dark night, (S,) in which the darkness confines men in their places of alighting or abode, and their shelter, so that they remain behind: or, as some say, such a night is termed ↓ مُغْدِرَةٌ because it casts him who goes forth therein into the غدر [i. e. غَدَر]. (L, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
